You are reviewing (not building) a colleague's already-open pull request on the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo — PR #84, "fix(app): remove placeholder DntNotification modal (SFCC-863)", author TimLavelleACC, branch `fix/SFCC-863-remove-dnt-placeholder-modal` → `develop`.

## What the PR does
Copy-first ports `overrides/app/components/_app/` (a Tier 2 "Global Shell" file per `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` — it did not exist as an override before this PR, base SFCC's `_app/index.jsx` was rendering unmodified on every tier) and removes the base template's `DntNotification` placeholder consent modal (Salesforce's own demo scaffolding — literal Lorem-ipsum body copy, no config flag to disable it). It also modifies `vitest.config.ts` (Tier 1 test config) to add two `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` subpath aliases (`/components`, `/page-designer`) ahead of the existing bare-specifier alias, and adds one ambient type declaration (`getRouterBasePath(): string`) to `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`.

## Jira ticket SFCC-863 (verbatim description)
"**Context** Surfaced while investigating SFCC-860's Lighthouse `categories.performance` finding (LCP 6.4s / score 0.1) against a real deployed build. The Largest Contentful Paint element turned out not to be an image — the homepage currently has none — but literal placeholder text inside a modal: 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...'. Traced to `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.js`'s `DntNotification` component, rendered unconditionally in the base `_app/index.jsx` — Zimmermann has no override for `_app` yet, so this base behaviour is live as-is on every tier. Salesforce's own source comment confirms it's not meant to ship: `// Placeholder for the consent tracking form for demonstration purposes`. It auto-opens via a `useEffect` whenever `selectedDnt === undefined` (i.e. on every fresh session with no stored preference) — confirmed no config-level toggle exists to suppress it.
**Why this matters beyond performance** Per AGENTS.md's Consent & Marketing section, Didomi is meant to own all consent gating for this project (REG-054, not-yet-started). This base component is not that — real shoppers on any tier without an `_app` override are currently seeing literal 'Lorem ipsum' copy in a tracking-consent dialog.
**Scope**
- Override `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` (Tier 2 — Global Shell, 'Both Squads — coordinate before touching' per protectedFiles.md; copy-first from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/index.jsx` per AGENTS.md's Copy-first rule) to stop rendering `<DntNotification>`
- Header and Footer are both already overridden — the new `_app` override must import them via relative paths (`../header`, `../footer`), not the base SFCC path, per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s 'Importing an already-overridden component' section, or Storybook/Vitest will silently exercise the unstyled base versions
- Decide how this interacts with the broader Didomi integration (REG-054) — does DNT tracking-consent get replaced by a Didomi-driven flow entirely, or does this story just remove the placeholder and Didomi work supersedes it later?
- Full TypeScript port of `_app` is non-trivial: ~500 lines, many hooks — budget real review time, not a quick patch
**Acceptance criteria**
- No placeholder/demo consent copy is ever shown to a real shopper on any tier
- Lighthouse's LCP on the homepage reflects real content, not this modal
- Header/Footer overrides continue to render correctly through the new `_app` override (spot-check Storybook and the real app, not just tsc)"

Note: SFCC-863's own Jira *summary/title* is "Suppress placeholder DntNotification modal; route consent through Didomi" — but the PR body explicitly states Didomi routing is out of scope, deferred to REG-054, "confirmed with the developer during planning." SFCC-863 has ZERO Jira comments recording that scope-narrowing decision anywhere. Worth independently assessing whether this scope call is defensible from the ticket body itself (it is arguably consistent with the ticket's own "Decide how this interacts..." open question) even though it's undocumented in Jira.

## Where to read the code
Two full git worktrees already exist locally, both with `node_modules` symlinked in and working (`npx tsc`/`npx vitest`/`npx eslint` all run fine from either):
- PR head (the actual PR content): `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/315b63a0-b125-4f80-a22b-5eb85ce56fd5/scratchpad/pr84-head`
- PR base (`develop` at the PR's merge-base, commit `9ab9aad`): `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/315b63a0-b125-4f80-a22b-5eb85ce56fd5/scratchpad/pr84-base`

Changed files (705 additions / 41 deletions total): `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` (471 lines, new), `overrides/app/components/_app/index.test.tsx` (175 lines, new), `vitest.config.ts` (modified, +22/-5), `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` (modified, +1), plus four auto-generated `.claude/registry/*.md` files (mechanical regen output from `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`, header says "do not edit manually" — low priority, only worth flagging if something looks hand-edited rather than regen-shaped).

## What I have ALREADY independently verified — do not redo, build on it
- tsc --noEmit: clean (exit 0) on both head and base.
- vitest: base = 45 files/678 tests all passing; head = 46 files/680 tests all passing (net +1 file/+2 tests = exactly the new `_app` suite, nothing else changed). PR body claims "47 files/682 tests" — that's off from my own measurement AND the CI bot's own PR comment (which says 680/680); flag as a minor/nitpick inaccuracy in the PR description only, not a functional issue.
- eslint on exactly the 4 real changed files: 0 errors, 3 warnings (all `@typescript-eslint/restrict-template-expressions`, `any` in a template literal at lines 326 and 376 of the new `_app/index.tsx`) — matches the PR body's claim exactly.
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`: byte-identical result on head and base except file-count (84 vs 83, the one new file) — exactly one pre-existing, unrelated violation (`footer/footer.css.ts:20`) on both sides. This PR introduces zero new token violations.
- I diffed the new `_app/index.tsx` line-by-line against `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/index.jsx` (the real base file) myself. Confirmed: `DntNotification`/`useDntNotification` import, hook call, and JSX render are the ONLY three removals — clean, surgical. Header/Footer/DrawerMenu/ListMenu are imported via relative paths (`../header`, `../footer`, `../drawer-menu`, `../list-menu`) exactly as the ticket requires, with a good explanatory comment. `PropTypes` correctly replaced by a TS `type AppProps`. Two `: any` usages (the `withCommerceSdkReact` render-prop closures) each carry an inline comment explaining why narrowing is out of scope for a copy-first port — compliant with `.claude/rules/typescript.md`'s any-needs-a-comment rule. One `usid ?? undefined` change (base was bare `usid`) — looks like a mechanical strict-null-checks fix now that this file is real TS, not a behavior change. One `watchOnlineStatus((isOnline) => ...)` param renamed to `online: boolean` — avoids shadowing the outer `isOnline` state var, correct type added. Several `// matches upstream base _app exactly.` comments added next to `useEffect` dependency arrays that would otherwise look like missing-deps bugs to a future reader — I read this as a deliberate, reasonable annotation given this is a faithful port, not a smell.
- The PR's claim "useAppOrigin was imported as a default import instead of the named export, which crashed SSR" does NOT show up as a delta in the diff — the base file already uses the correct named-import form (`import {useAppOrigin} from ...`), same as the new file. This means either the claimed bug was real but transient (introduced and self-corrected before the one squashed commit landed) or the narrative is embellished — I cannot tell which from the artifact, and there's only one commit on the PR so there's no intermediate state to inspect. Flag as unverifiable-from-diff if you can't find other evidence either way; don't assert it's false, since the end state is correct regardless.
- `vitest.config.ts`: new subpath aliases (`/components`, `/page-designer`) are correctly ordered BEFORE the pre-existing bare `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` alias entry (Vite matches bare-specifier keys as a prefix, so order matters — confirmed correct, and the PR's own comment explains this accurately).
- `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`: adds `getRouterBasePath(): string` — I confirmed this file is the FIRST TS file in `overrides/` to import `getRouterBasePath` from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/ssr/universal/utils`, so the ambient declaration was previously simply missing, not wrong. (I'm separately checking the real SDK's actual exported signature myself — don't spend time on that.)
- CODEOWNERS: `overrides/app/components/_app/` requires approval from `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a`, `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`, `@ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers`, OR `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (any one). `vitest.config.*` requires `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. I confirmed via `gh api` that TimLavelleACC (the PR author) IS a real member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` and holds repo admin — so his identity-verification claim for the `vitest.config.ts` edit is TRUE and procedurally correct per AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval section. Separately, I confirmed via the PR's own review thread that CodeRabbit correctly flagged that his OWN reply ("I am a Tier1 approver... so this is approved given I have made the change") does NOT satisfy the Tier 2 Global Shell requirement for `_app/`, because (a) GitHub structurally does not allow a PR author to submit an "Approved" review on their own PR, and (b) protectedFiles.md's Global Shell rule calls for a developer other than the author / cross-squad coordination, which is a different gate than Tier-1-approver status. As of now the PR has zero human approving reviews (only a CodeRabbit bot approval) and is not mergeable. I don't need you to re-litigate this governance finding — it's my primary finding already. What WOULD be useful: is there anything in the code itself (not the process) that specifically warrants a second squad's eyes — i.e., does this `_app` port touch anything Squad B (if you can determine squad boundaries from `.claude/rules/` or CODEOWNERS) would specifically care about, beyond the generic "it's shared shell" concern?
- The PR's git-merge status against current `develop` tip is CONFLICTING, but I traced it: the only real conflicts are inside the four auto-generated `.claude/registry/*.md` files (timestamp + consumer-count diffs from an unrelated, already-merged PR #82/SFCC-708 touching PDP colour swatches) — mechanically resolved by rebasing and re-running `node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`. No substantive logic conflicts. Just confirm you agree nothing else conflicts if you happen to check `vitest.config.ts`/`vendor.d.ts`/`_app/*` against current `develop` tip.

## What I actually need FROM YOU (don't re-verify the above, dig into what I haven't covered)
1. **Test mock fidelity** — the new `_app/index.test.tsx` mocks roughly 30 modules via `vi.mock(...)`. For each mock, check whether the mocked shape (default export vs named export, function signature) actually matches what the real module exports (cross-check against `node_modules/@salesforce/...` and `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` in either worktree's `node_modules`). A mismatched mock shape (e.g. mocking a named export as a default export) would make the test pass while silently not exercising the code path it claims to.
2. **Anything else in the 471-line `_app/index.tsx` port I might have missed** — re-diff it yourself against the real base file at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/_app/index.jsx` (in either worktree) and look specifically for anything beyond what I listed above: a reordered prop, a changed default value, a dropped null-check, an altered conditional. Prettier reformatting (quotes/semicolons/line-wrapping) is irrelevant noise — ignore it.
3. **Failure modes / security** — anything about the new file's SSR path, the `getRouterBasePath`/`getAssetUrl` usage, or the Page Designer wiring that could fail silently or behave differently between SSR and client hydration now that this is a real TS override instead of the untouched base file.
4. **Squad-boundary code check** — see the CODEOWNERS note above.
5. Anything about the `.claude/registry/*.md` diffs that looks hand-edited rather than tool-generated (spot check one or two).

I am running the visual/browser verification myself (there's a live MRT preview URL) — that's not your job. Report findings only; don't fix anything. Keep it tight — this is a small, well-scoped PR, not a sprawling one.

## Methodology note No sub-agent/Task tool is available in this environment, so I could not literally dispatch parallel sub-agents. I worked each angle below as a separate, adversarial pass against the artifacts myself (reading real `node_modules` source, hitting the GitHub API directly rather than trusting descriptions) rather than fanning out — flagging this since the standing instructions assume fan-out is possible. ## Headline finding: the worktree I was given is not the PR's actual current head `gh pr view 84 --json headRefOid` → `da8c37036d03d0fcaaffeb586573d20d9bf9ae63`. The `pr84-head` worktree's `git rev-parse HEAD` → `50871bf...` — **one commit behind the real tip**. The missing commit is a merge of `develop` into the branch. I fetched all six PR-changed files at the real tip via `gh api .../contents/?ref=da8c37036...` and diffed against the worktree: - `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`, `vitest.config.ts`, `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts` — **byte-identical** to the worktree. Every finding below about these four files is unaffected by the staleness. - `.claude/registry/components.md` and `.claude/registry/hooks.md` — **not identical**. This is where it matters (next section). **CONFIRMED.** This means Marcel's own registry-conflict assessment ("mechanically resolved by rebasing and re-running `generateRegistry.mjs`... no substantive logic conflicts") was made against a pre-merge snapshot and does not hold for the PR as it actually stands right now. ## Angle: `.claude/registry/*.md` — real, unresolved corruption on the actual PR head (🟡 should-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM) At the true tip (`da8c37036`), both touched registry files carry duplicated, conflicting content — this is the exact defect CodeRabbit's second review flagged as 🟠 Major ("Both files append a second older registry snapshot"), and it is **still present**, contradicting the PR's own final "APPROVED" CodeRabbit review: - `components.md` lines 3-4: two `> Last updated:` lines (`2026-09-04T00:54:34.181Z` and `2026-09-02T10:17:24.916Z`). - `components.md` lines 12-13: two conflicting rows for `App` — one says `Override | overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx | ... | 21` consumers, the other says `Base | app/components/_app/index.jsx | ... | 7` consumers. **This is the literal subject of this PR** — the registry now asserts both that `_app` is and isn't overridden. - `components.md` lines 28/40 (`Header`, consumers 63 vs 54) and 117/125 (`ZimmIcon`, consumers 10 vs 9) — same row duplicated with stale counts. - 32 distinct component names duplicated total (`App`, `Header`, `Footer`, `ZimmIcon`, `ZimmButton`, `DrawerMenu`, etc.); `hooks.md` has 4 (`useEinstein` lines 33/34: 2 vs 1 consumers; `useToast` lines 73/74: 2 vs 0 consumers). This isn't cosmetic: `.claude/skills/feature-spec/SKILL.md` ("Agent A — Registry / file scan") reads `components.md`/`hooks.md` as its primary source of truth instead of grepping the codebase — a future planning session asking "is `_app` already overridden?" gets a contradictory answer from the very file built to answer that. **UNIFORM** because nothing enforces idempotency/uniqueness on this generator's output today — any future PR whose merge touches the registry is exposed to the same botched-resolution shape; this isn't a one-off typo, it's a process gap. ## Angle: Imports — base-path import of an already-overridden component (🔴 must-fix, CONFIRMED, UNIFORM) `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:49`: ```ts import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/responsive'; ``` `overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx` **is** a real Zimmermann override, and it is not a cosmetic port — it deliberately changes the mobile/desktop split from Chakra's default `lg` (992px) to `md` (768px), with a comment explaining this fixes "a dead zone between 768-991px where content wrapped in both helpers was simultaneously hidden." `_app/index.tsx` uses these two exactly to wrap `DrawerMenu`/`ListMenu` inside `
` (lines ~405-424). The test file's own mock (`index.test.tsx:82-85`) mocks the same wrong base path, so `npm run test` stays green — the mock launders the bug rather than catching it. This is precisely the failure mode the ticket named for Header/Footer/DrawerMenu/ListMenu and the PR fixed for those four — just missed for a fifth already-overridden dependency in the same file. Blast radius today: zero in production (webpack's `ccExtensibility` resolver redirects either path form correctly) and zero in the current test suite (mock matches the wrong import), but live the moment anyone adds a Storybook story for `_app` (none exists yet) or writes a test that doesn't mock `responsive`. **UNIFORM**: the same shape (base-path import of an override that changes real behavior) already exists as a separate, pre-existing, unrelated bug in `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (confirmed via `git diff --stat 9ab9aad HEAD` — not touched by this PR, so not this author's doing, but corroborates this is a repeatable codebase mistake pattern worth a dedicated sweep). **Related but lower-severity, 🔵 note, CONFIRMED:** `_app/index.tsx:75-83` imports `CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_NAV_SSR_DEPTH, CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY, DEFAULT_LOCALE, DEFAULT_SITE_TITLE, HOME_HREF, STORE_LOCATOR_IS_ENABLED, THEME_COLOR` from the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants` path, even though `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` exists. I read that override's content: it's `export * from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants'` plus one new constant (`CUSTOM_HOME_TITLE`) — a pure superset, no redefinition of any of the 7 names `_app` imports. So, unlike `responsive`, **there is currently no value divergence** — I checked rather than assumed. It's also the established repo-wide pattern already (6 other pre-existing files do the same base-path import), so this is consistent with existing practice, not something introduced by this PR. Flagging only because it becomes a live bug the day `constants/index.ts` ever redefines one of those 7 names instead of just re-exporting it. ## Angle: Test mock fidelity (~30 `vi.mock()` calls) — clean, CONFIRMED I cross-checked every mock in `index.test.tsx` against the real exported shape in `node_modules` (named vs. default, function vs. value): - Subpath re-export chains verified by reading the actual compiled files: `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/components` → `StorefrontPreview` (real, via `ShopperExperience`/`StorefrontPreview` barrel); `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/page-designer` → `PageDesignerProvider` (real, via `ShopperExperienceV2` barrel); `useCategory` from the bare `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` specifier initially looked unexported (0 grep hits in `hooks/index.js`) until I traced the dynamic `Object.keys(_ShopperProducts).forEach(...)` re-export at `hooks/index.js:250-258` — it's real, just not a literal string in the bundle. `useAccessToken`, `useShopperBasketsMutation`, `useUsid` all confirmed the same way. - `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils`'s mock (`index.test.tsx:130-136`) adds an extra `noop` entry beyond what `_app` itself imports, with a comment claiming it's needed because `constants.js` imports `noop` transitively. I verified this is real (`utils.js:62` exports `noop`, `constants.js:9,191` imports and uses it in an object literal), though the specific "would crash" framing is slightly overstated — an undefined `onPrimaryAction` in an unused config object wouldn't throw, it'd just silently be wrong. The mock entry is still shape-correct and harmless. `isServer` is correctly mocked as a boolean (`isServer: true`), matching the real `export const isServer = typeof window === 'undefined'` — not a function, which the naming could tempt someone to get wrong. - Header/Footer/DrawerMenu/ListMenu override export shapes all confirmed to match both the component's real import style and the test's mock (`Header`/`Footer` default-only, `DrawerMenu` named, `ListMenu`/`ListMenuContent` named). No shape mismatches found anywhere in the ~30 mocks. This was a genuine, non-trivial verification (had to trace two levels of Babel-compiled re-export indirection for the commerce-sdk-react package) — reporting it as checked-clean, not skipped. ## Angle: Re-diff of `_app/index.tsx` against real base — one additional undocumented change found Beyond the three `DntNotification` removals, `PropTypes`→`AppProps`, `usid ?? undefined`, and the `isOnline`→`online` rename Marcel already found, I found one more: **`index.tsx:370`**, the `hrefLang` map callback parameter was renamed from `locale` to `l: { id: string }` (base line 366 shadows the outer `const {site, locale, buildUrl} = useMultiSite()` binding with its own `.map((locale) => ...)`). Functionally identical — the renamed param is used the same way inside the callback — but it's a second unmarked shadow-avoidance rename alongside the `isOnline`/`online` one, and neither carries a comment the way `usid ?? undefined` self-explains as a strict-null-checks fix. 🔵 note, CONFIRMED, ONE-OFF. No other functional deltas found beyond what Marcel already listed — I re-read every line of both files side by side. On the disputed **"`useAppOrigin` was a default import, crashed SSR"** claim: I checked one more angle Marcel didn't — the commit message on `50871bf` (`gh pr view --json commits`) describes the DntNotification removal and the `vitest.config.ts` fix in detail but **does not mention the `useAppOrigin`/SSR bug at all**. That's mildly odd for something framed as "a real bug found during local verification," but proves nothing either way since there's only one substantive commit. Still unverifiable from any artifact in the repo — flagging as PLAUSIBLE-but-unproven per your instruction, not false. ## Angle: SSR / hydration failure modes - **DntNotification removal is hydration-safe, CONFIRMED.** Its own `useDntNotification()` hook only calls `onOpen()` inside a `useEffect` (base `use-dnt-notification.jsx:33`), which never runs during SSR — so the modal never rendered visible content server-side even before this PR. Removing it introduces no new server/client markup mismatch. - **Inherited (not introduced) latent bug, PLAUSIBLE:** `pageDesignerMode` (`index.tsx:178-184`) is a `useMemo` reading `location.search` but keyed only on `[req?.url]`. `req` comes from `useServerContext()` and is server-only — on the client it's always `undefined`, so the dependency never changes across re-renders after hydration, and the memo freezes at its mount-time value. A shopper navigating client-side to a URL with `?mode=EDIT`/`?mode=PREVIEW` after initial load would not get Page Designer mode updated. This is byte-identical to the base file (correctly preserved, and honestly labeled `// matches upstream base _app exactly.`) — not a regression from this PR, but now that `_app` is a real Zimmermann-owned TS file rather than untouched vendor code, this is a latent bug the team now owns rather than inherits silently. Worth a ticket, not a blocker on this PR. - 🔵 FYI, pre-existing, out of scope: `commerceAgentConfiguration?.enabled === 'true'` (`index.tsx:379`) compares to the string `'true'`, not a boolean — identical in base, not this PR's doing. ## Angle: Squad-boundary code check (direct answer to your question) Read `.claude/rules/squadA.md` / `squadB.md`. Squad B's explicit territory is `pages/search/`, `pages/account/`, `pages/store-locator/`, `components/search/`, `components/store-locator/`, plus `use-derived-product`/`use-variant`/`use-wish-list`. Beyond the generic "shared shell" concern, `_app/index.tsx` contains real logic Squad B should specifically look at: - `onWishlistClick`/`onAccountClick` (lines 308-312, 302-306) route into `pages/account/` — Squad B territory. - `useStoreLocatorModal`/`` (lines 165-169, 390) wires open/close state for `pages/store-locator/` + `components/store-locator/` — both explicitly Squad B's. - `activeData.trackPage(site.id, locale.id, currency)` fired on every route change (lines 316-323) — squadB.md's own charter header is "Discovery, **Localisation & Analytics**" and explicitly lists "SEO & analytics" as a future Squad B area. - The root category tree (`useCategory` + `CAT_MENU_DEFAULT_ROOT_CATEGORY`) feeding `DrawerMenu`/`ListMenu` is Squad A-owned per squadA.md's frontmatter, but the tree itself powers site-wide discovery navigation — worth Squad B's awareness even if not their file. Conversely, `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer` + the two basket-currency/customer-email sync `useEffect`s (lines 238-247, 254-265) and the `isCheckout` → `CheckoutHeader`/`CheckoutFooter` swap are squarely Squad A (cart/checkout) logic. So both squads have concrete, non-generic reasons to review this file, not just "it's shared shell" boilerplate — which corroborates CODEOWNERS' "both squads" tagging on `_app/` being substantive rather than a placeholder. ## Other angles — checked, clean or not applicable - **Tokens/styling conformance:** read the full file myself; no raw hex/px/rem/em, no bare Chakra token keys, no new `.zimm-*` classes. This file composes existing styled components rather than authoring new styles — angle is vacuous for this PR, consistent with Marcel's `audit:tokens` byte-identical result. - **Recipe state exhaustiveness:** not applicable — no new recipe or interactive part introduced. - **Structure:** `AppProps` name matches convention; test file correctly co-located as `index.test.tsx`. `export default App` with no named export matches the established SFCC-bridge default-export-only pattern already used by `header/index.tsx` (also default-only) — not a violation. **No `.stories.tsx` exists for `_app`** — technically required per components.md ("any component exported from its folder"), but `_app-config` (the only structurally comparable root-shell file in the repo) also has no story, so this reads as an existing, unwritten precedent for app-shell wiring components rather than an oversight unique to this PR. 🔵 note. - **Accessibility:** no new ``, `IconButton`, or non-native `onClick` introduced; `SkipNavLink`/`SkipNavContent` landmarks preserved unchanged. - **Intra-step DRY:** no constant/literal duplicated across `index.tsx`/`index.test.tsx` that risks drift. - **Against the ticket ACs:** AC1 (no placeholder copy) — satisfied, all three touchpoints removed, regression-guarded by the mock-spy test.
